Here the limits of the numerator and denominator are ${lim}_{x\to 0}{e}^{2/{x}^{2}}=\infty $ and ${lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}}=\infty ,$ respectively, so we have the case $\frac{\infty }{\infty }.$

Applying L'Hopital's rule, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{{e}^{2/{x}^{2}}}{(\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}})} & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{{[{e}^{2/{x}^{2}}]}^{′}}{{[\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}}]}^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{{e}^{2/{x}^{2}}(-\frac{4}{{x}^{3}})}{(-\frac{1}{{x}^{3}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{4{e}^{2/{x}^{2}}\cancel{(-\frac{1}{{x}^{3}})}}{\cancel{(-\frac{1}{{x}^{3}})}} \\  & =4{lim}_{x\to 0}{e}^{2/{x}^{2}} \\  & =\infty .\end{aligned}
$$
